item.title: Special report: PeakQi's team AI城市起風 wins the Land Office track at New Taipei's AI Smart City Hackathon

item.title: AI CRM vs traditional CRM: the real difference, in one table
item.description: A traditional CRM stores what you type; an AI CRM turns conversations into records and schedules the next step. One table, plus when the old CRM is enough.

item.title: n8n, packaged SaaS or a custom AI platform? Ask first: who fixes it when it breaks
item.description: All three can wire AI into a process; the difference is who keeps it running. Compared on operations, data, cost of change and human handoff.

item.title: What AI automation costs a small business, and how long it takes to launch
item.description: Setup fee, monthly fee and usage cost, broken apart: what drives each one, how to estimate the timeline, and what makes a project more expensive.

item.title: How to choose an AI automation partner in Taiwan: six questions to ask first
item.description: Choosing an AI automation vendor isn't about the feature list — it's process, data, human review and exit terms. Six questions to ask before signing.

item.title: Connecting LINE AI support to your CRM: from first enquiry to an automatic record
item.description: AI on a LINE Official Account solves half the problem: if the chat never reaches your CRM, follow-up still runs on memory. Four links, four breaks.

item.title: I hadn't written code in ten years. I built a website with Claude Code.
item.description: I can write code, but I hadn't in ten years. I work in animation, but I can't produce assets. 414 commits across 16 working days, one person, a 32-page bilingual company site. This is the working record — including the day I got stuck, what I threw away, and one solution I didn't see coming.
